redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 6 of 1022 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - ck1 (house FAIL), ck2 (house FAIL), ck3 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 1016/1022 cases passed; --case ck4 names no case that failed an assertion in this run; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: init.md's mode rule covered only bug->tdd, refactor->regression, config->gate-only; a task that adds or changes observable behaviour (a feature, the common case) fell through to the silent `mode = args.tests_mode or "gate-only"` default in audit-task.py's _build_task. Added `_change_kind_discipline(title, description)` (new regexes _REFACTOR_TEXT, _CONFIG_TEXT) in plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py: when a task names no --tests-mode and no stronger signal (a bug, a --fixes target, an inline-suite tests.add) has already answered, _build_task now reads the task's own title+description and classifies regression (refactor/restructure/cleanup/hardening text), gate-only (config/docs/document/mechanical text), or tdd otherwise (expectRedFirst true) -- with the basis recorded as a task note. This is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in flag: no new CLI flag or mode value was added, and an explicit --tests-mode always wins (ck4, ALLOW case). Applies uniformly to `add` and to `/audit:phase add --from-file` batch tasks naming no tests.mode, since both route through _build_task. Updated commands/init.md (step 3's mode rule), reference/execute-task.md and agents/audit-executor.md (tdd discipline: draft tests.add from the task's own text before reading the implementation) and reference/manifest-conventions.md to document the default. Fixed fallout in plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: t1/t3 (the 'New guard' task now classifies tdd, carrying one note), dg1/dg2 and the scope-inline fixture in _inline_suite_mode_cases now pass --tests-mode gate-only explicitly since those cases test gate/scope behaviour unrelated to mode classification, is2 updated to expect the new tdd default, and _batch_doc's second task given an explicit tests.mode (gate-only) to avoid a timestamped classification note making two independent subprocess writes (fb13, file vs stdin) non-byte-identical. Added _change_kind_discipline_cases (stage ck-block, cases ck1-ck4) exercising the default directly. Verified: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest` -> ALL PASS: 1022/1022 cases passed (exit 0); full `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` in the task tree -> 332/332 files ok, 15948 cases (exit 0).
outcome.descriptive: A planned task naming no test mode is now classified tdd/regression/gate-only from its own text instead of silently defaulting to gate-only, with the basis recorded on the task.
